          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. This appeal arises from the judgment and order passed by
the High Court of Judicature at Bombay dated 22 December, 2023
by which the writ petition preferred by the respondent no.2
before us seeking a writ of Habeas Corpus came to be allowed.
2. The facts, in brief, giving rise to this appeal are as
2

--- Page 51 ---
Crl. Appeal  No. 2564/2024
under:-
(i) The appellant before us and the respondent no.2
are husband and wife.  They got married in India on
25–10–2014.   The  respondent  no.2  is  an  Indian
citizen  by birth  and presently  residing in  the
United States of America (USA), and is a green card
holder and permanent resident of the USA.  In the
wedlock, a daughter was born on 14 December, 2018 in
the USA. The daughter is a citizen of the USA.
(ii) It appears from the materials on record that
some differences arose between the husband and wife
in the US.  The appellant before us has levelled

REPORTABLE
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Civil Appeal  No(s).  13229/2026
(arising out of SLP(C) No. 11670/2023)
SECRETARY, DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH & ANR.             Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
SUDHA BATTA & ORS.                                 Respondent(s)
WITH
Civil Appeal No. 13230/2026
(arising out of SLP(C) D. No. 17960/2023)
AND
Civil Appeal No. 13231/2026
(arising out of SLP(C) No. 11668/2023)
AND
Civil Appeal Nos. 13232-13233/2026
(arising out of SLP(C) D. No. 21171/2023)
O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Leave granted. 
3. The seminal issue falling for consideration in this batch of
appeals  is  whether  the  term  degree  mentioned  in  the
Advertisement/Rules would mean, “Bachelor's Degree” only, or it
would include, “Master's Degree” also vis-a-vis qualification for
1

--- Page 77 ---
the post of Food Safety Officer.
4.  An Advertisement was issued by the Himachal Pradesh Staff
Selection Commission for filling up various posts, including 19
posts of Food Safety Officer, (in short, “FSO”). 
5.  As  per  the  Advertisement,  the  minimum  qualification
prescribed for the post of FSO was as under:
657
Food Safety Officer
i) A Degree in Food Technology or Dairy
Technology  or  Biotechnology  or  Oil
Technology or Agricultural Science or
Veterinary Sciences or Bio-Chemistry or
Microbiology  or  Master's  Degrees  in
Chemistry or Degree in Medicine from
recognized University; or
ii)  Any  other  equivalent/recognized
qualification notified by the Central
Government; and
iii)  Has  successfully  completed
training  as  specified  by  the  Food
Authority in a recognized institute or
institution approved for the purpose.
Provided that no person who has any
financial interest in the manufacture,
import or sale of any article of food
shall be appointed to be a Food Safety
Officer under this rule.
6. The petitioners before the High Court, who are respondents
herein, are having “Master's Degree” in Biotechnology/Microbiology.
Their candidature was rejected on the ground that they did not have
the “Bachelor's Degree” in Biotechnology/Microbiology, although,
they had “Master's Degree” in Biotechnology/Microbiology. Learned
Single Judge of the High Court dismissed their writ petition,
against which writ appeals were preferred, which has now been
allowed  and  the  appellant,  Himachal  Pradesh  Staff  Selection
Commission (Rajya Chayan Aayog) has been directed to consider the
2

--- Page 78 ---
cases of the writ petitioners for the post of FSO, and if they are,
otherwise found to be eligible, and their names find place in the
merit, then they be appointed to the post of FSO.
7. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants have argued to
persuade us to take a stand that the respondents, having not
obtained a “Bachelor's Degree” in the concerned subject, they would
not be eligible to apply for the post. 
8. However, in view of the law laid down by this Court, in
Chandra Shekhar Singh and Others v. The State of Jharkhand and
Others (  CIVIL APPEAL NO(S). 10389 OF 2024  , the issue no longer
remains res integra. In Chandra Shekhar Singh (supra) this Court was
dealing with the same post for which the Advertisement was issued
in the State of Jharkhand. Having examined the provisions contained
in Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, and the rules framed
thereunder, particularly, Sections 37, 91 and 94 of the Act, and
Rule 2.1.3 of the Food Safety and Standard Rules, 2011, (in short,
“FSS Rules, 2011”), this Court held thus in paragraphs 27 to 32
which are reproduced hereunder:
“27. The Central Government, while exercising powers under
Section 91 of the FSS Act notified the Food Safety and
Standard  Rules,  2011  wherein,  the  educational
qualifications for the post of the FSO have been provided
as under:-
“2.1.3: Food Safety Officer 
1. Qualification: Food Safety Officer shall be a
whole time officer and shall, on the date on which
he is so appointed possesses the following:
(i)  a  degree  in  Food  Technology  or  Dairy
Technology or Biotechnology or Oil Technology or
Agricultural  Science  or  Veterinary  Sciences  or
3

--- Page 79 ---
Bio-Chemistry or Microbiology or Master’s Degree
in  Chemistry  or  degree  in  medicine  from  a
recognized University, or
(ii) any other equivalent/recognized qualification
notified by the Central Government, and
(iii)  has  successfully  completed  training  as
specified by the Food Authority in a recognized
institute or Institution approved for the purpose.
 
Provided that no person who has any financial interest
in the manufacture, import or sale of any article of
food shall be appointed to be a Food Safety Officer
under this rule.”
28. These very rules have been adopted by the State of
Jharkhand mutatis mutandis. It is in this background, that
we are required to adjudicate whether the term ‘degree’ as
mentioned in the rules and the recruitment notification can
be restricted to “Bachelor’s degree” or whether the same
would cover in its ambit, the “Master’s degree” as well.
29. The term ‘degree’ is defined under Section 22(3) the
UGC  Act,  which  states  that  the  ‘degree’  means  the
‘Bachelor’s Degree’, ‘Master’s Degree’ and the ‘Doctorate
Degree’. Thus, wherever the word ‘degree’ is used, unless a
specific exclusion is provided, the same would include
within its scope and ambit all three, ‘Bachelor’s Degree’,
‘Master’s Degree’ and a ‘Doctorate Degree’.
30. In the present case, the respondents have disqualified
the appellants on account of the fact that they hold
Master’s degree in different subjects whereas, as per
Clause 2.1.3 of the FSS 2011 Rules (supra) and the subject
advertisement, the educational qualification of a master’s
degree is only recognized in “Chemistry” subject, whereas
for all the other subjects, only a graduation degree would
be the qualifying criterion.
31. We feel that there is no ambiguity whatsoever in the
FSS 2011 Rules or the subject advertisement which can
exclude the Master’s degree in subjects referred to in the
preceding part of the Rule 2.1.3 of the FSS 2011 Rules
(supra),  other  than  Chemistry,  as  being  a  valid
qualification. The special reference to the Master’s degree
is given in the said Rule, only for those who have acquired
their degree course in Chemistry subject, for whom, the
minimum qualifying criterion will be a Master’s degree in
Chemistry. However, so far as the other subjects are
4

--- Page 80 ---
concerned, a person having any degree, be it graduation or
post-graduation, would be equally qualified for the post in
question.
32. Reading the language of the statutory provision in a
literal  sense  and  applying  the  golden  rule  of
interpretation, this is the only logical and permissible
interpretation. Hence, we have no hesitation in concluding
that if a candidate, having undertaken a degree course in
“Chemistry” subject, desires to apply for the post of FSO,
he must possess a master’s degree in that subject. However,
if a candidate has taken college education in the subjects
of food technology; dairy technology; biotechnology; oil
technology;  agricultural  science;  veterinary  science;
biochemistry or microbiology, then such a candidate would
be qualified for the FSO post, if he holds any one of the
degrees,  i.e.,  either  graduation,  post-graduation  or
doctorate degree in any of these subjects. There is no
logic or rationale behind excluding the candidates having
master’s or a doctorate degree in these subjects from
staking a claim to the post of FSO because such an
interpretation  would  be  totally  unjust,  arbitrary  and
unconstitutional.”
9.  Having said so, this Court held in conclusion, in paragraph
34,  that  the  appellants,  therein,  who  possessed  postgraduate
degrees in subjects covered under Rule 2.1.3 of the FSS Rules,
2011, are qualified for the post of FSO. This Court, thereafter,
passed the following operative order, as contained in paragraph 35
which are reproduced hereunder:
“35. Resultantly, the appeal is allowed in the following
manner :-
i. The impugned judgments rendered by the Division Bench
and the Single Bench, holding that the appellants were
not qualified for the post of FSO, are quashed and set
aside.
ii. The prayer made by the appellants to appear in the
interview under the Advertisement No. 18 of 2023 dated
15th June, 2023 issued by JPSC, cannot be acceded to as
they did not apply under this advertisement.
iii. In order to do complete justice, and in case
5

--- Page 81 ---
vacancies do not exist in the recruitment process 2016,
then the respondents shall create supernumerary posts to
accommodate  the  appellants  who  shall  be  allowed  to
partake in the recruitment process from the stage they
were disqualified, i.e., from the interview stage. In
case after undergoing interviews, the appellants succeed
and are placed at par or higher in merit as compared to
the last successful candidate in the particular category,
they  shall  be  offered  appointment  which  shall  be
effective from the date of publication of the first
select list in the recruitment process 2016. We further
clarify that since the selected candidates were never
impleaded and heard in the proceedings before the High
Court or in this Court, appropriate direction has to be
given to ensure that their seniority position is not
disturbed  at  this  belated  stage.  It  is,  therefore,
provided that the successful candidates from amongst the
appellants shall be placed below the last candidate
selected and appointed in the subject selection process.
iv. It is further clarified that in case the appellants
succeed and are offered appointment, they shall not be
entitled to back wages. However, they shall be entitled
to all service benefits on a notional basis.”
10. In the present case also, the respondents are having “Master's
Degree” in Biotechnology/Microbiology. Thus, their case is squarely
covered by Chandrasekhar Singh (supra).
11. In view of the above settled legal position, we affirm the
order passed by the High Court and direct the appellant(s) and the
State of Himachal Pradesh to appoint the respondents to the post of
FSO subject to their otherwise being eligible and their name
finding place in the merit. It is made clear, we have not
interfered with the appointment already made pursuant to the
subject selection process and that the seniority of the respondents
shall be reckoned just below the candidates who are already
appointed.
6

--- Page 82 ---
12. With the above observations, these appeals are accordingly,
disposed of.
13. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of. 
......................J.
(PRASHANT KUMAR MISHRA)
......................J.

                                VERSUS

O R D E R
Leave granted.
This criminal appeal challenges the order dated
22.07.2025 passed by the High Court of Jharkhand
at Ranchi, in I.A. No.8275/2025 Criminal Appeal
(DB)  No.695/2023,  whereby  the  appellant’s
application  for  suspension  of  sentence  was
dismissed.
The appellant faced trial in connection with a
crime registered pursuant to P.S. Case No.12/1997
dated 17.02.1997 lodged with P.S. Nagar Untari in
respect of the offences punishable under Sections
147, 148, 149, 302, 120B of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (“IPC”) and under Section 27 of the Arms Act,
1959 (“Arms Act”).
The trial court in Sessions Trial No. 217/2014,
1

--- Page 103 ---
convicted the appellant herein for the offences
under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC
and under Section 27 of the Arms Act vide judgment
dated  03.04.2023  and  awarded  a  sentence  of
rigorous imprisonment for life, along with a fine
of Rs. 20,000/-, for the offence under Section 302
read with Section 149 of IPC, and a sentence of
rigorous imprisonment for a period of 3 years,
along with a fine of Rs. 1000/-, for the offence
under Section 27 of the Arms Act. The sentences
were directed to run concurrently.
Aggrieved, the appellant filed Criminal Appeal
(DB)  No.  695/2023  before  the  High  Court  of
Jharkhand at Ranchi and the same is pending before
the High Court. During the pendency of the said
criminal  appeal,  the  appellant  filed  an
application bearing I.A. No. 8275/2025 before the
High Court seeking suspension of sentence. The
High  Court,  by  the  impugned  order  dated
22.07.2025, dismissed the application filed by the
appellant for suspension of sentence. Hence, the
2

--- Page 104 ---
present criminal appeal.
This Court  vide  its order dated 17.09.2026,
issued notice in the instant matter.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned counsel for the respondent(s)-State and
perused the material on record.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted
that in the case of Rajendra Yadav and another vs.
State of Jharkhand arising out of SLP (CRL.)
No.1266  of  2026,  this  Court  by  order  dated
13.04.2026 granted the relief of bail to those
appellants. The appellant herein is also a senior
citizen  aged  about  sixty  eight  years  and  is
similarly  placed  to  the  appellants  in  the
aforesaid  case.  In  the  circumstances,  the
aforesaid order may be followed in the present
case also and the relief of bail may be granted to
the appellant herein.
Per  contra,  learned  counsel  for  the
respondent(s)-State contended that with reference
to the counter affidavit contended that there is
3

--- Page 105 ---
no merit in this appeal also and the same may be
dismissed.
Considering the facts on record and following
the aforesaid order dated 13.04.2026, we grant the
relief of bail to the appellant herein.
We, therefore, allow this appeal and direct as
under:
“The appellant shall be produced before the
concerned trial Court as early as possible, and
the trial Court shall release him on bail, subject
to such conditions as it may deem appropriate to
impose to ensure his presence in the proceedings.”
The appellant shall appear before the High
Court as and when directed to do so.
It is directed that the appellant shall extend
complete cooperation in the hearing of the appeal
before the High Court. 
The appellant shall not misuse his liberty in
any manner.
Any infraction of the conditions shall entail
cancellation of the suspension of sentence granted
4

--- Page 106 ---
to the appellant.
With these observations, the criminal appeal is
allowed.

Leave granted.
This  appeal  challenges  the  order  dated
08.04.2026 passed by the High Court of Judicature
at  Patna  in  Criminal  Miscellaneous  No.20016  of
2026. 
The present criminal appeal arises in connection
with the crime registered pursuant to FIR No.540 of
2022 dated 24.10.2022 registered at Police Station
Jokihat (Mahalgaon), District Araria in respect of
offences punishable under Section 30(a) of Bihar
Prohibition  and  Excise  Act,  2016.  Anticipating
arrest in connection with this crime, the appellant
preferred Criminal Miscellaneous No.20016 of 2026
1

--- Page 110 ---
before  the  High  Court  of  Judicature  at  Patna
seeking anticipatory bail.
This application for anticipatory bail having
been rejected by the High Court vide impugned order
dated  08.04.2026,  the  instant  appeal  has  been
preferred.
Vide  order  dated  03.08.2026,  while  issuing
notice, this Court granted interim protection in
favour of the appellant.
We have heard learned counsel for the appellant
and learned counsel for the respondent-State.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that
pursuant to the interim order dated 03.08.2026 the
appellant  has  been  cooperating  with  the
investigation;  that  other  persons  who  are  also
alleged in the same FIR have been granted the
relief of regular bail. The appellant is a fifty
one year old lady and merely because she was the
owner of the truck from which the codeine substance
mixed  cough  syrup  was  seized,  she  has  been
proceeded with although she has no connection with
the alleged offence. In the circumstances, this
Court may set aside the impugned order and grant
2

--- Page 111 ---
the relief of anticipatory bail while making the
interim order absolute subject to the terms to be
imposed.
Per  contra , learned standing counsel for the
respondent-State  with  reference  to  the  counter
affidavit contended that there is no merit in this
appeal and the same may be dismissed.
Considering the circumstances on record, in our
view, the appellant is entitled to the relief of
anticipatory bail sought by him.
We, therefore, allow this appeal and set aside
the impugned order passed by the High Court of
Judicature at Patna dated 08.04.2026. We direct
that in the event of arrest of the appellant, the
Arresting Officer shall release the appellant on
bail, subject to furnishing cash security in the
sum of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty-Five Thousand
only) with two like sureties.
It is directed that the appellant shall extend
complete cooperation in the ensuing trial. 
The appellant shall not misuse her liberty and
shall not in any way influence the witnesses or
tamper with the material on record.
3

--- Page 112 ---
With  the  aforesaid  directions,  the  criminal
appeal is allowed.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
INHERENT JURISDICTION
CONTEMPT PETITION (C) No.503 OF 2024
IN
CIVIL APPEAL No.5827 OF 2023
SAVITA KASHYAP                   … PETITIONER
VERSUS
INDRA MANI TRIPATHI & ORS.      … RESPONDENTS
O  R  D  E  R
1. The instant Contempt Petition has been filed by the petitioner alleging that the State
had failed and/or neglected to pass an enhanced award under the provisions of the Right to
Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement
Act, 2013 by treating the market value of the land as on 01.01.2014.
2. Mr. Nidhesh Gupta, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the contemnors,
had during the hearing of the matter contended that his clients had serious reservations
whether petitioner was the lawful owner and had the right to receive the enhanced
compensation as directed.  In view of this objection, vide order dated 12th September
2025, we directed the District Judge, Lucknow to hold a judicial enquiry and submit a report
with regard to the genuineness of the sale deed dated 10.2.1972, executed in favour of the
predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner. Pursuant to our direction, report of the District
Judge has been filed. Though, an opportunity was given to the contemnors to rebut the
said report, no such objection came to be filed, but the contemnors have sought to place on
record various documents to cast a cloud on the title of the petitioner. Mr. Gupta, learned
Senior Counsel, strenuously argues apart from such documents, the District Judge's report
itself brings on record certain irreconcilable issues, namely, the volume number 1536, in
which the sale deed dated 10.02.1972 is said to be registered, was not being used in 1972,
and that the stamp paper in which the deed had been executed also had not been

--- Page 131 ---
2
contemporaneously purchased.  
3. After considering relevant materials the District Judge opined in the report as follows:
“a) The original sale-deed dated 10.02.1972 is not available on
record and its photo-copy is on record and on the basis of photo-
copy, mutation proceedings were carried out and on the basis of
photo-copy only, the respective orders with regard to grant of
compensation have been passed in favour of claimant.
b) As per record, land in question was initially recorded in the name
of Late Captain Umrav Singh (in Khatauni fasli year 1376-1379) and
after his death, his three sons namely Manmohan Gupta, Anand
Mohan Gupta and Krishna Mohan Gupta inherited the property and
mutation thereof in their favour took place. Further, Manmohan Gupta
died and after his death, his son Ravindra Mohan and Nileema
Gupta, widow of Arvind Mohan, inherited his share.
c) Lucknow Development Authority was not the erstwhile owner of
land in question and it acquired the land for development of
Ujariyaon Housing Scheme Phase-1 in the year 1986. From the
date of acquisition, L.D.A. or any other person including the legal-
heirs of the deceased Anand Mohan Gupta and Krishna Mohan
Gupta never challenged the title of claimant over the property till the
order passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Contempt Petition (Civil)
No. 503 of 2024. Various writ petitions were filed by legal-heirs of
Manmohan Gupta and claimants before Hon'ble High Court where
L.D.A. was party but L.D.A. neither disputed the title nor alleged the
sale-deed being forged one.
d) Ravindra  Mohan  and  Nileema  Gupta  were  granted
compensation to the tune of Rs. 2,22,998/- each in 2006 for their
respective 1/6th share in the property by LDA after filing Writ
Petition No. 48 (L.A.) of 1997 before Hon'ble High Court.
e) Neither Anand Mohan Gupta nor Krishna Mohan Gupta nor
their legal heirs approached any forum/authority/court seeking
compensation or claiming right over 2/3rd share in the property in
question.
f) Claimant's husband Rakesh Kumar got his name mutated on
04.06.2014 in respect of 2/3rd share in land in question through
succession on the basis of sale-deed dated 10.02.1972 stated to be
executed by aforesaid Anand Mohan Gupta and Krishna Mohan
Gupta in favour of his father Ram Kumar @ Raj Kumar (deceased).
The mutation order dated 04.06.2014 passed by Naib Tehsildar
concerned was never challenged by any person including the legal-
heirs of deceased namely Krishna Mohan Gupta and Anand Mohan
Gupta and the said order was recalled on 23.11.2024 on the basis
of objection filed by L.D.A. claiming the sale-deed being a forged
one. Claimant's husband Rakesh Kumar was granted compensation

--- Page 132 ---
3
for his 2/3rd share in the property to the tune of Rs. 11,23,926/- on
07.09.2015 after filing Writ Petition Land Acquisition No. 127/2014
before Hon'ble High Court.
g) In the opinion of the undersigned, it was well within the
knowledge of Ravindra Mohan, who is son of Manmohan Gupta
who was real brother of Anand Mohan Gupta and Krishna Mohan
Gupta and legal heir of Late Captain Umrav Singh, and Nileema
Gupta (widow of Arvind Mohan) that 2/3rd share in the property has
been sold off by Anand Mohan Gupta and Krishna Mohan Gupta as
they both being real family members and they approached Hon'ble
High Court claiming compensation of only 1/3rd share in the
property and no one from their family turned up before any
authority/forum/court seeking compensation or claiming title on
remaining 2/3rd share.
h) Office of the Sub-Registrar produced six Jilds/Volumes which
were in use in the year 1972 but failed to produce the entire record of
Jilds/Volumes and Syaha Register in use despite the order passed by
the Inquiry Officer which demonstrates there is some concealment on
the part of Sub-Registrar concerned.
i) Thus, on the basis of entire facts and circumstances narrated
above and perusal of record, in my considered opinion, the report of
concerned Record Keeper sent to Lucknow Development Authority to
the effect that Volume No. 1536 was not in use in the year 1972, on
the basis of which L.D.A. has claimed that sale-deed is forged/not-
genuine, is not sufficient to hold that sale-deed in question is forged
particularly when the parties of sale-deed or their legal-heirs have not
challenged or disputed the sale-deed nor did L.D.A. ever challenge
the veracity of deed or title of claimant prior to disbursing the
compensation amount as per old Act nor did concerned Sub-
Registrar office where the said sale-deed is stated to be executed
lodged an complaint thereof nor L.D.A. could provide any proof with
regard to alleged forgery.
j) There is no proof whether documentary or ocular, other than
mere assertion on the part of L.D.A., which, in no manner
whatsoever, can be assumed to be sufficient to prove allegation of
alleged  forgery,  hence,  the  objections  raised  by  Lucknow
Development Authority are found to be misconceived, unsupported
by evidence, filed at such belated stage and devoid of any legal
merit and title of the property in question is in favour of claimant on
the basis of alleged sale-deed.”
4. We have given anxious consideration to the submissions of Mr. Gupta and have
perused the additional documents placed on record in rebuttal of such report. It is true that
there are certain inconsistencies with regard to the maintenance of volume number 1536 in
the concerned department wherein the registration of the deed had been recorded.  But it

--- Page 133 ---
4
has not been denied that one Captain Umrav Singh and thereafter his lawful heirs, namely,
Manmohan Gupta, Anand Mohan Gupta, and Krishna Mohan Gupta, were the owners of
the said property. Said Anand Mohan and Krishna Mohan are said to have sold their share
in the property vide sale deed dated 10.02.1972 to one Ram Kumar @ Raj Kumar
(deceased father of Rakesh Kumar i.e., husband of the petitioner). In 2014, the property
was mutated in favour of said Ram Kumar. District Judge has rightly recorded nothing has
been placed on record to show that the signatures in the registered sale deed are forged.
More  importantly,  Lucknow  Development  Authority  (“ LDA”)  had  already  granted
compensation to the petitioner’s late husband and other co-sharers with regard to the same
acquisition and only belatedly in 2024 raised this dispute resulting in correction of mutation
made in favour of late Ram Kumar.  That apart the registered sale deed is more than thirty
years old and carries a presumption of genuineness.1  We are also cognizant that this issue
is being agitated in a contempt proceeding whose scope of enquiry is limited, and would
not permit us to go behind the order already passed by this Court.
5. In these circumstances, we have no reason to come to a contrary view than that
opined by the District Judge concerned and we are of the view that the petitioner is entitled
to receive the enhanced amount deposited with the registry of this court.  
6. In light of the aforesaid discussion, we are of the opinion though no case of willful
and deliberate violation of the order has been made out against the contemnors to attract
any punitive measure, we direct that the amount deposited with the Registry with interest
accrued thereon be released to the petitioner within two weeks subject to the petitioner
furnishing an undertaking before this Court that she shall refund the said sum to the LDA in
the event any competing claim with regard to such compensation is made and allowed by a
competent court of law. 
7. Finally, Mr. Gupta contends that the LDA who has deposited the said sum may be
1  Section 92 of BSA

--- Page 134 ---
5
given liberty to recover such amount from the beneficiaries concerned.
8. Keeping in mind the nature and scope of the proceeding, we merely record his
submission without expressing any opinion thereon.
9. The Contempt Petition is disposed of accordingly.
10. As a result, the pending interlocutory application also stands disposed of.

            (JOYMALYA BAGCHI)
 ..………….….....……………….…....J.

2026 INSC 1085
1
REPORTABLE
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Civil Appeal No(s).  13004/2026
(Arising out of SLP (C) No. 513/2026)
GOPAL PATHAK                                       APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
NITIN ALIAS PAPPU & ANR.  
R-1: NITIN ALIAS PAPPU
R-2: OMPRAKASH
                           RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
Heard  Ms.  Neelakshi  Bhadauria,  learned  counsel  for  the
appellant  and  Ms.  Tanya  Raizada,  learned  counsel  for  the
respondents.
2. Leave granted.
3. The challenge in the appeal is to the order dated 27.10.2025
passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Gwalior in M.P. No.
5813/2025, by which the High Court has overturned the decision of
the Trial Court. It is pertinent to note that the Trial Court had
rejected the prayer of the respondents-tenant for sending the
“Will” in question to the handwriting expert on the ground that it
was competent to take a call on the same. However, the High Court,
by the impugned order, has held that sending the “Will” in question
to the handwriting expert is ‘ essential’ for determining the

--- Page 150 ---
2
genuineness of the same.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the High Court
failed to appreciate that the Second Sale Deed dated 20.10.1981
expressly records that the father of the respondents was a tenant.
He emphasises that the respondents have admitted the said second
sale deed dated 20.10.1981 in their application under Section 39 of
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. He contends that the respondents
cannot be permitted to simultaneously rely upon and repudiate the
same document. 
5. He points out that the application for expert opinion was
filed  by  the  respondents  four  years  after  trial  proceedings
commenced  in  2020  and  after  recording  of  petitioner’s  and
respondents’  evidence.  He  contends  that  permitting  an  expert
examination at this stage would reopen the entire evidentiary
process.
6. He submits that the approach of the High Court is erroneous as
it is the discretion of the Court whether to decide the matter
itself, or for assistance, send it to an expert and to take a final
call based on the opinion. 
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent submits that the
“Will” was not a genuine document and thus the only remedy left to
the respondents was to make a request to the Court for sending it
to a handwriting expert for comparison, which has rightly been
upheld by the High Court. Learned counsel relied on a decision of
this Court in the case of Thiruvengada Pillai v. Navaneethammal &

--- Page 151 ---
3
Anr. (2008) 4 SCC 530 , the relevant portion being at paragraph No.
16, to contend that where there is a dispute with regard to
handwriting/signature/finger impression, the opinion or finding by
the Court could be hazardous and risky and therefore the matter
should be sent to an expert.
8. We have heard the parties at length. The short point involved
is whether it would be ‘essential’, as has been held by the High
Court, to send the document to obtain expert opinion under Section
39 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 for determining the
genuineness of the Will or whether the same can be ascertained by
comparison in accordance with Section 72 of Bharatiya Sakshya
Adhiniyam, 2023, which is reproduced hereinbelow: 
72. Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or
proved.
(1) In order to ascertain whether a signature, writing or seal is that of
the person by whom it purports to have been written or made, any signature,
writing, or seal admitted or proved to the satisfaction of the Court to
have been written or made by that person may be compared with the one which
is to be proved, although that signature, writing or seal has not been
produced or proved for any other purpose.
(2)The Court may direct any person present in Court to write any words or
figures for the purpose of enabling the Court to compare the words or
figures so written with any words or figures alleged to have been written
by such person.
(3)This section applies also, with any necessary modifications, to finger
impressions.
9. Having considered the matter, we find that the impugned order
cannot be sustained.
10. This Court is of the view that the law gives discretion to the
Court concerned to form an opinion as to whether it would itself
compare the signatures on its own or seek an expert opinion.
11. This Court is further of the view that it is the duty of the
Court to compare the signature or writing and come to its own

--- Page 152 ---
4
conclusion and the same cannot be avoided by recourse to a
statement that the Court is not an expert. In fact, the evidence of
an expert is only an opinion which is not binding on the Court.
Consequently, the finding of the High Court that obtaining expert
opinion under Section 39 of the Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is
essential for determining the genuineness of the Will is untenable
in law. However, the Court has full discretion to seek expert
opinion like where it has any doubt or the writing/impression is
smudgy, vague or very light.
12. Furthermore, what was disputed and compared in  Thiruvengada
Pillai v. Navaneethammal & Anr. (2008) 4 SCC 530,  was a finger
impression and not a handwriting or signature. This Court is
therefore of the view that the observation of this Court at
paragraph  no.  16  of  judgment  in  Thiruvengada  Pillai  v.
Navaneethammal & Anr. (2008) 4 SCC 530 cannot be read to mean that
it is essential to examine an expert witness in all cases which
involve a disputed handwriting/signature/finger impression.  
13. We find no infirmity in the view taken by the Trial Court.
Further, what is ultimately held by the Trial Court is always
amenable to further challenge by the party aggrieved.
14. Accordingly, on a short point as discussed above, the appeal
is allowed. The order impugned is set aside. The order of the Trial
Court dated 06.10.2025 passed by the 12 th Civil Judge, Junior
Division, District Gwalior in RCSA No. 577A/2020 stands restored.
However, the Court observes that the matter being one of eviction,

--- Page 153 ---
5
the  same  be  expedited  and  taken  to  its  logical  conclusion
expeditiously in accordance with law.
15. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
......................J.
(AHSANUDDIN AMANULLAH)
......................J.
(MANMOHAN)
NEW DELHI
SEPTEMBER 18th, 2026

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.        OF 2026
(Arising out of SLP (Criminal) No. 14020 of 2026)
BHOLA ALIAS MAHESH CHANDRA APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
THE STATE OF U.P.        RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The present appeal arises out of the impugned order
dated 23.04.2026 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Allahabad in Criminal Appeal No. 332 of 2026, whereby the
application for bail/suspension of sentence filed by the
appellant was rejected.
3. The facts of the case reveal that the appellant has
been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 412
of the IPC1, and has undergone approximately two years and
two months of the sentence awarded to him.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits
that the looted goods were allegedly recovered at the
instance of the appellant from the premises of the owners
1 . Indian Penal Code, 1860
1

--- Page 174 ---
of Om Chemical Tiles Factory. The said factory owners were
also arrayed as co-accused in the case and have been
convicted for the offence punishable under Section 412 of
the IPC. It is submitted that, in the case of the said co-
accused, the High Court has already suspended the sentence
awarded to them. It is, therefore, submitted that the
appellant is also entitled to the benefit of parity.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent-State
has  vehemently  opposed  the  prayer  for  suspension  of
sentence, contending that the appellant is not entitled to
the benefit of parity, as it was the appellant who had
allegedly sold the looted goods to the other co-accused
persons.
6. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and
have perused the material available on record. Taking into
consideration the period of incarceration already undergone
by the appellant and the fact that the sentences of the
other co-accused persons, who have also been convicted
under Section 412 of the IPC, have already been suspended,
we are of the view that the appellant is also entitled to
relief on ground of parity.
7. Accordingly, the impugned order passed by the High
Court is set aside.
8. The  execution  of  the  sentence  awarded  to  the
2

--- Page 175 ---
appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of the
appeal before the High Court, subject to such terms and
conditions as may be imposed by the Trial Court.
9. The High Court is requested to take up and decide
the pending criminal appeal at an early date, preferably
expeditiously.
10. The appeal is allowed in the aforesaid terms.
11. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
TRANSFER PETITION(S) (CIVIL) NO.   1451/2026  
DASARI @NAGULAKONDA ARAVINDA SUPRAJA & ANR.      Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
GANESHAN KRISHNAN & ORS.                         Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. The present petition has been filed seeking transfer of
Motor Vehicle Claim Petition, viz., Motor Vehicle OP No. 1147
of 2024, titled as  “Nagulakonda Aravinda & Another vs.
Ganeshan & 4 Others” , pending before the court of 14 th
Additional  Chief  Judge,  City  Civil  Court,  Hyderabad,
Telangana, to Principal District Judge Court, Vizianagaram,
Andhra Pradesh.
2. The petitioner is the wife of the deceased, whereas the
claim petition pending before the Court at Hyderabad has been
instituted by the parents of the deceased.
3. Learned Amicus Curiae, appointed by this Court to assist
the parents of the deceased, submits that the parents are
elderly  persons  and  are  unable  to  undertake  travel  to
Vizianagaram to attend each and every date of hearing. It is
further submitted that the claim petition instituted by the
parents at Hyderabad was filed prior in point of time,
1

--- Page 184 ---
whereas the petitioner subsequently instituted a separate
claim  petition,  being  M.V.O.P.  No.  203  of  2024,  at
Vizianagaram.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that
the petitioner is employed as a Senior Resident Doctor and is
suffering from certain medical ailments, on account of which
the transfer of the claim petition has been sought.
5. It is undisputed that the accident occurred at Hyderabad,
Telangana, and that the relevant records and witnesses are
available at Hyderabad. It is also not in dispute that the
claim petition instituted by the parents was filed earlier in
point of time.
6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and upon
consideration of the circumstances of the case, this Court is
of the considered view that M.V.O.P. No. 203 of 2024 ought to
be heard and decided along with M.V.O.P. No. 1147 of 2024, so
as to avoid multiplicity of proceedings and the possibility
of conflicting findings.
7. Accordingly, M.V.O.P. No. 203 of 2024, titled  “Smt.
Dasari @ Nagulakonda Aravinda Supraja & Another v. Ganeshan &
4 Others”, pending before the Court of the Principal District
Judge, Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh, is hereby transferred to
the Court of the XIV Additional Chief Judge, City Civil
Court, Hyderabad, Telangana, where M.V.O.P. No. 1147 of 2024
is pending.
8. The  record  of  M.V.O.P.  No.  203  of  2024  shall  be
2

--- Page 185 ---
transmitted to the transferee Court forthwith and without any
unnecessary delay.
9. A copy of this order be sent to the concerned court for
compliance. If video conferencing facility is available with
the transferee Court, the benefit of the same shall be
extended to the parties on such dates when their physical
appearance is not required. It is made clear that this Court
has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the matter.
10. The parties are directed to appear before the transferee
court on 16.10.2026.
11. The transferee Court shall permit the petitioner to
appear and depose through video conferencing in the event
that she is unable to attend the proceedings physically,
subject to such directions as may be issued by the Trial
Court in accordance with law.
12. Since it has been brought to the notice of this Court
that the office of the Presiding Officer of the concerned
Court is presently vacant, the Hon’ble the Chief Justice of

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.         OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO. 16109 OF 2026)
DHARAM DEV                                         PETITIONER(S)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF HARYANA & ANR.                            RESPONDENT(S)
R1 STATE OF HARYANA
R2 VIPIN KUMAR
O R D E R
Heard Mr. Rahul Shukla, learned counsel for the
petitioner,  Mr.  Lokesh  Sinhal,  Senior  AAG  for  the
respondent  no.1-State  of  Haryana  and  Mr.  Samay
Sandhawalia, learned counsel for the respondent no.2.
2. Leave granted.
3. The  present  appeal  arises  out  an  order  dated
09.07.2026 passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana
at Chandigarh in CRM-M-21043-2026 (O & M), by which the
respondent no.2 has been granted anticipatory bail.
4. The respondent no.2 is accused of participating in
the assault of the deceased which led to his death.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the
respondent no.2 has two other criminal antecedents and is
convicted in one under Section 302 of the Indian Penal
1

--- Page 189 ---
SLP (CRL.) NO. 16109/2026
Code, 1860 and in the present case also, the CCTV footage
shows that he is actually involved in the commission of
the offence. Thus, learned counsel submitted that the
High  Court  order  granting  anticipatory  bail  to  the
respondent no.2, was totally unjustified.
6. Learned Senior AAG for the respondent no.1-State of
Haryana submits that the custodial interrogation of the
respondent no.2 is required as he has not cooperated in
the investigation and the State had also opposed the
prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the respondent
no.2 before the High Court.
7. Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 submits that
the respondent no.2 is innocent and, in fact, he has
intervened only because the incident was happening in
front of his house and to prevent the matter from
escalating, he had gone there and he had separated the
parties and then immediately he came back to his house
and after that there is no role attributed to him. It was
further submitted that the respondent no.2 has no concern
with the other accused as also the person who died and
further, he was not even aware of who the persons were.
8. On a quick response, learned counsel for the State
of Haryana submits that the respondent no.2 has been
named to be a friend of the person who had given the
fatal blow and thus, he could not claim ignorance either
2

--- Page 190 ---
SLP (CRL.) NO. 16109/2026
with regard to the incident taking place, or of his
involvement in commission of the offence.
9. Having considered the matter in its entirety, we
agree with the submissions of learned counsel for the
appellant that in the facts and circumstances of the
case, grant of anticipatory bail to the respondent no.2
was not proper.
10. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed. The impugned
order is set aside and the anticipatory bail granted to
the respondent no.2 stands cancelled. The respondent no.2
is directed to appear before the Court concerned within
two weeks from today.
11. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

(AHSANUDDIN AMANULLAH)

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
Miscellaneous Application Diary No.34075/2026
In 
Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No.1497 of 2017
GAYADHAR JENA   
                          ……Applicant
VERSUS
THE STATE OF ODISHA 
……Respondent(s)
O R D E R
The  applicant  is  in  custody  for  not  having
complied with the order of this Court and seeks
modification of the directions issued by this Court.
This  Court,  on  11.07.2017,  passed  the  following
order: -
“We are informed that a deposit of Rs. 14 Lakhs
(Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Only) has already been
made by the petitioner. So, the balance amount
of Rs. 4 Crores and 36 Lakhs (Rupees Four
Crores and Thirty-Six Lakhs Only) shall be
deposited by the petitioner within a period of
six months from today. In case, the balance
amount is not deposited within the period as

--- Page 199 ---
mentioned aforesaid, it would be open to the
respondent-State  of  Odisha  to  take  the
petitioner into custody again.”
2. The applicant has not complied with the same despite
time granted subsequently. The applicant has already
been taken into custody. We are not inclined to modify
the  order  passed  by  this  Court  on  11.07.2017,
especially in view of the undertaking given by the
applicant.
3. The learned Counsel for the applicant, then points out
that the applicant is in custody and cannot move an
application for bail since the order passed by this
Court stands in his way.  He has been in custody for
long and the trial has not commenced even now. It is
also pointed out that he is unable to raise the money,
because the properties he owned has been attached by
the Court trying the case.  
4. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case,
we are of the opinion that the applicant could move a
regular bail application, pointing out these facts
before the appropriate Court which shall consider the
prayer, untrammeled by the directions issued by this

--- Page 200 ---
Court in 2017 which has not been complied with. The
circumstances  of  long  incarceration,  delay  in
commencement  of  trial  and  the  attachment  of  the
properties made; which the applicant submits is valued
far in excess of the liability, if at all, mulcted on
him, could be considered in such a bail application by
the appropriate Court. 
5. With  the  above  observations,  the  Miscellaneous
Applications stands disposed of. We make it clear that
we have not made any observation on the applicant’s
eligibility to bail, which is at the discretion of the
Court before which it is prayed.      
…………………………………………J.
                                  (J. B. PARDIWALA)
…………………………………………J.
                           (K. VINOD CHANDRAN)
NEW DELHI;
OCTOBER 01, 2026.

                             O R D E R
1. The  petitioner before  this Court  has filed  the
present petition, being aggrieved by the impugned order
dated 25.03.2026 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Allahabad in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application
U/S 482 BNSS No. 1171 of 2026, rejecting the prayer for
anticipatory bail in connection with FIR/Case Crime No. 205
of 2025, registered at Police Station Pipari, District
Sonbhadra,  for  the  offences  punishable  under  Sections
318(4), 319(2), 336(3), 338, 340(2), 351(3) and 352 of the
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
2. In the present case, the petitioner and respondent
No. 2 are real brothers, and the dispute pertains to the
management and control of a society registered under the
Societies Registration Act, 1860.
3. Various allegations have been levelled against the
petitioner.
4. A Coordinate Bench of this Court, vide order dated
20.04.2026, had granted interim protection in favour of the
petitioner, which has been extended from time to time.
5. The order sheets reveal that an attempt was also
made by this Court to resolve the dispute through mediation
before the Registrar (Societies), however, the mediation
has failed.
2

--- Page 205 ---
6. Learned counsel for the respondent-State has opposed
the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail, submitting that
it is a case of forgery and, therefore, bail should not be
granted.
7. Learned counsel appearing for respondent No. 2 has
submitted  that  the  petitioner  has  forged  an
affidavit/general body minutes, which was notarized on a
date when the mother was not alive.
8. Pursuant to the interim directions passed by this
Court, the petitioner has joined investigation and appeared
before the Investigating Officer as well as the Registrar
(Societies) as directed from time to time.
9. This Court, keeping in view the totality of the
circumstances of the case, the fact that the dispute
pertains to the control of a society, and also considering
that the petitioner and respondent No. 2 are real brothers,
is of the opinion that the interim order dated 20.04.2026
deserves to be made absolute.
10. Accordingly, interim order dated 20.04.2026 is made
absolute subject to the condition that petitioner shall
continue to co-operate with the investigation and shall
report  as  and  when  called  upon  to  do  so  by  the
Investigating Authority.
11. The Special Leave Petition is accordingly disposed
3

--- Page 206 ---
of in the above terms.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand
disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
(Criminal Appeal No.   /2026)
(Arising out of SLP (Crl.)  No.13010/2026)
SACHIN ARJUN LAKAL & ORS.                          Appellants
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF MAHARASHTRA & ANR.                    Respondents
O R D E R
1. Heard.
2. Leave granted.
3. The Petitioners who came to be tried for the offences punishable under
Sections 353, 332, 323, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code,
1860 (IPC) were convicted for the offence punishable under Section 323 read
with Section 34 of IPC and sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for a
period of six months with a fine of Rs. 1000/- each with a default sentence of
simple imprisonment for a period of 15 days and they were acquitted for the
other offences i.e., offences under Sections 353, 332, 504 and 506 read with 34
of IPC.
4. The said Order dated 03.08.2023 came to be affirmed by the Appellate
Court by the impugned order/judgment dated 02.04.2026.
5. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on
perusal of the records, we are not inclined to interfere with the order of the
conviction and same stands affirmed.
1

--- Page 212 ---
6. Having regard to the fact that petitioner No.1 is suffering from Carcinoma
as evident from the medical certificate furnished by Dr. Anand Deshmukh
(Radiologist) and taking into consideration that all the petitioners seem to have
expressed remorse for the act perpetrated by them, we are of the considered
view that it would be apt and appropriate to modify the sentence to the period
already undergone and accordingly, the judgment stands modified and the
present appeal stands disposed of.
7. Pending application(s), if any, stands consigned to records.

                   Ms. Tejal Tapaswani Nagauri, Adv.
                   
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. This matter has come up today to consider the plea of the
petitioner (convict) for suspension of sentence of rigorous
imprisonment for life with a fine of Rs.15,000/-, and release on
bail, pending the final disposal of the matter before the High
Court.
2. It is alleged that on 06.03.2014, the Petitioner along with
other co-accused committed the murder of one Naresh Kumar
wherein the Petitioner is arrayed as First accused in the FIR
for inflicting a gunshot wound on the deceased.
3. We take notice of the fact that the petitioner was put to
trial for offences punishable under Sections 302, 148 & 149 of
the Indian Penal Code, 1860 along with Sections 25, 54 and 59 of
the Arms Act, 1959.
4. The Trial Court, relying on the consistent statements of
PW-5 and PW-6, held the petitioner & co-accused guilty of the
alleged crime and sentenced the Petitioner to undergo rigorous
imprisonment for life and to pay fine of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees
SLP(Crl.)  No.8860/2026        2

--- Page 233 ---
Fifteen thousand rupees only), and in default, to undergo
rigorous imprisonment for a period of one year, in Sessions Case
No.34/2015.
5. Being dissatisfied with the dismissal of his suspension of
sentence application by the High Court dated 03.02.2026, the
petitioner filed this Special Leave Petition before us.
6. We take note of the fact that the petitioner has been in
jail for more than 12 years.
7. On a prima facie consideration, we are of the opinion that
the  sentence  imposed  on  the  petitioner  can  be  suspended
considering  his  prolonged  period  of  incarceration  and  the
pending appeal before the Punjab & Haryana High Court.
8. In view of the aforesaid, we suspend the substantive order
of sentence of rigorous imprisonment for life imposed on the
petitioner and order that the petitioner be released on bail
forthwith, if not required in any other case, subject to terms
and conditions that the Additional Sessions Judge, Hoshiarpur
may deem fit to impose, pending the final disposal of his appeal
before the High Court.
9. With the above directions, the Special Leave Petition is
disposed of.
SLP(Crl.)  No.8860/2026        3

10. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed
of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL No.     OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) No.10811/2026)
RAJENDRA SINGH ..... APPELLANT(S)
            
               VERSUS
STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. In this appeal, appellant has assailed the order
dated 18.04.2026 passed by the High Court of Madhya
Pradesh at Indore (briefly the ‘High Court’ hereinafter)
rejecting the bail application of the appellant.
4. Appellant has been named as an accused in Crime
No.294 of 2024, registered at Police Station Suvasara in
the District of Mandsaur (Madhya Pradesh) under Section
103(1) read with Section 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita, 2023 (for short, ‘BNS’).
5. As per the prosecution, the nephew of the informant
1

--- Page 248 ---
did not return home from the paddy field on 27.10.2024.
When the informant along with another person went to the
field, he found his nephew in an injured condition lying
on the ground. He was taken to the hospital where he was
declared brought dead.
6. Appellant was arrested on 13.11.2024 and has been in
custody since then.
7. It is a case of circumstantial evidence.
8. Vide  order dated 08.06.2026, this Court had issued
notice. In the proceedings held on 15.09.2026, we were
informed by the learned State Counsel that out of 33
prosecution witnesses, 31 were already examined. Next
date  fixed  for  hearing  was  19.09.2026.  This  Court
directed that on the next date, i.e., on 19.09.2026, the
remaining two prosecution witnesses should be examined.
9. In  the  hearing  today,  learned  counsel  for  the
appellant submits that though one witness was examined,
prosecution has decided to bring back one more dropped
witness to testify. Thus, as of today, there are still
two prosecution witnesses left to be examined. In this
way, the trial would take some time for conclusion.
10. Learned State counsel on the other hand submits that
the two remaining witnesses are police officials who were
assigned duty for the Ganesha festival because of which
their depositions could not be recorded.
11. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on
due consideration, particularly the nature of allegations
2

--- Page 249 ---
and evidence against the appellant, we feel that further
custody of the appellant may not be warranted.
12. Accordingly, we set aside the impugned order of the
High Court dated 18.04.2026 and direct that appellant
shall be produced before the Jurisdictional Sessions
Court within a maximum period of 7 days from today
whereafter he shall be released on bail on such terms and
conditions as may be deemed appropriate.
13. We further direct that appellant shall cooperate with
the  Trial  Court  and  not  seek  any  unnecessary
adjournments.
14. Appeal is accordingly allowed.
15. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
......................J.
(UJJAL BHUYAN)
......................J.
(ATUL S. CHANDURKAR)

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL No.     OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) No.15785/2026)
MITESHGIRI @ MULRAJGIRI 
SEVAGIRI GOSWAMI & ANR. 
..... APPELLANT(S)
            
               VERSUS
THE STATE OF GUJARAT ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. The two appellants before us are husband and wife.
While appellant No.1 was a Principal in Shri Secondary
School, Vekaria, appellant No.2 was the President of the
governing body of the said school.
4. Allegation  against  the  appellants  is  that  of
tampering with the service record of the first appellant
to change the date of birth from 19.06.1964 to 19.06.1965
thereby resulting in change in his date of retirement.
Further allegation is that because of such change in
dates, appellant No.1 has made unlawful gain at the cost
1

--- Page 252 ---
of the public exchequer. In this connection, a First
Information  Report  (FIR)  was  registered  being  CR
No.11203070250475  of  2025  with  the  Visavadar  Police
Station, District Junagarh under Sections 316(5), 336(2),
336(3),  340(2)  and  61(2)(a)  of  the  Bharatiya  Nyaya
Sanhita, 2023 (for short, ‘BNS’).
5. Application  for  anticipatory  bail  filed  by  the
appellants was rejected by the High Court of Gujarat at
Ahmedabad (briefly the ‘High Court’ hereinafter) vide the
order dated 16.06.2026.
6. This Court by order dated 25.08.2026 had issued
notice and passed an interim order to the effect that
appellant should not be arrested in connection with the
aforesaid case subject to them cooperating with the
investigation.
7. Pursuant to such order, State of Gujarat has filed
affidavit which we have perused.
8. Considering the nature of allegation against the
appellants which are all based on documents, we are of
the view that custodial interrogation of the appellants
is not necessary. That apart, appellant No.1 is a senior
citizen having retired as Principal of the school.
9. However, our attention has been drawn to paragraph 11
of the impugned order of the High Court dated 16.06.2026
which reads thus:
11. In view of the above decision and
in view of the facts and circumstances of
2

--- Page 253 ---
this case, custodial interrogation of not
only  the  applicant,  but  all  other
suspect/s  is  therefore  imperative  to
unearth the truth. Hence, this is not a
fit case to exercise the jurisdiction in
favour of the applicant.
10. We are of the firm view that it is not for the High
Court to suggest any form of interrogation of an accused.
This should be best left to the discretion of the
investigating agency. By such sweeping observation that
custodial interrogation of not only the applicant but all
other  suspects  is  imperative,  the  rights  of  other
‘suspects’ have been jeopardized. The High Court should
avoid making such unnecessary observations.
11. Consequently, we set aside the impugned order of the
High Court dated 16.06.2026 and make our order dated
25.08.2026  absolute  with  the  further  direction  that
appellants  shall  continue  to  cooperate  with  the
investigation.
12. Appeal is accordingly allowed.
13. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
......................J.
(UJJAL BHUYAN)
......................J.
(ATUL S. CHANDURKAR)
NEW DELHI;
September 30th, 2026.

 SHAILESHKUMAR BABUBHAI MALIYA                     RESPONDENT
O R D E R
1. This is a petition filed under Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure,
1908. The petitioner has filed this Transfer Petition seeking the following reliefs:
"Transfer the Matrimonial Case No. FSUIT No.2137/2025, titled
as ‘ Shailesh  Kumar  Babubhai  Maniya  v.  Bhawana  Shailesh
Kumar  Maniya’ , pending before the Court of S.V. Mansuri,
Judge, Family Court, Surat, Gujarat to the Court of PJFC, District
Shahdara, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi."
2. We have heard the learned counsel for both the parties. 
3. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and on perusal of the
material on record, we find that the petitioner has made out a case for transfer
of the aforesaid petition. 
4. In the result, the Transfer Petition is allowed and Matrimonial Case No.
FSUIT No.2137/2025, pending before the Court of S.V. Mansuri, Judge, Family
Court, Surat, Gujarat is hereby transferred to the Court of PJFC, District
Shahdara, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.
1

--- Page 286 ---
5. Registry to communicate this order to the transferor court for taking
steps in accordance with this order. 
6. On an application made by the respondent, the Court to which the case
is transferred shall permit the respondent to appear through video-conference
on all dates except on the dates on which his personal presence is absolutely
mandatory.
7. The transfer petition stands allowed in the aforesaid terms. 
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

Court in connection with FIR Case No. 661/2024 filed at PS
Haringhata, District Nadia for the offences punishable under
Sections  20(b)(ii)(C),  25  &  29  of  Narcotic  Drugs  and
Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985.
2. It is alleged that petitioner is the owner of vehicle (WB 86G
5781) which was seized along with 41.100 Kgs of Ganja. Further
it is alleged that A1/co-accused stated to have paid rent to
the owners of the vehicles for using them in commission of the
crime. It is also alleged that the owners of the vehicle had
previously supplied the vehicle for carrying ganja.
3. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that co-accused (A1
and A2), who were specifically named in the FIR, were granted
regular bail by the Hon’ble High Court and thus seeks parity. 
4. Hence on a prima facie consideration of the material on record
SLP(Crl.)  No.17677/2026               2

--- Page 305 ---
and considering that the chargesheet is filed on 13.06.2025,
we are of the opinion that the petitioner can be released on
anticipatory bail.

connection with the offence enumerated above, they shall be
released on bail, subject to such terms and conditions that
the  Investigating  Officer  (for  short  “I.O.”)  or  the
jurisdictional court may deem fit impose, on condition also of
continued cooperation in the investigation. 
6. Once the aforesaid petitioner is released on bail by the I.O.,
on directions issued by the I.O. or summons issued by the
Additional District & Sessions Judge, I st, Krishnanagar, Nadia
(the jurisdictional court), the petitioner shall appear before
the jurisdictional court and furnish bail bonds and ensure due
appearance in the trial.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA 
       CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
 
 
CIVIL APPEAL NO(S).  7871 OF 2024 
(Arising out of SLP (C) No. 32995 OF 2018) 
 
 
  
HINDUSTAN CABLES LIMITED & ANR.      …APPELLANT(S) 
 
                                  VERSUS 
 
 K SRI RAMASHARMA & ORS.                 …RESPONDENT(S) 
 
 
 
O R D E R  
 
 
1. The present appeal challenges the order dated 
20.11.2018 passed by the High Court in a Writ Appeal 
whereby the benefit of revised pay scales have been granted 
to the respondent(s) with effect from 01.01.1997 to 
31.03.2001 on having opted for and allowed voluntary 
retirement. 
2. It may be noted here that respondent No(s). 1, 3, 12 
and 17 have since expired and no application for 
impleadment of their legal representatives has been filed by 

--- Page 322 ---
C.A. No.  7871 OF 2024          2 
the appellant(s). Vide order dated 13.01.2020, the Special 
Leave Petition qua them was ordered to be abated. In the 
absence of any application for impleadment of their legal 
representatives till date, the appeal(s) qua respondent(s) No. 
1, 3, 12 and 17 shall stand abated and the judgment under 
challenge in this appeal has attained finality for them.  
3. We have heard the learned counsel(s) appearing for the 
parties at length. It is an undisputed fact that similarly 
situated employees, who had sought voluntary retirement 
and were so permitted, were released pay revision benefits 
in terms of the decision of the appellant -Company, 
pursuant to the judgment passed by the High Court. 
4. The said judgment when challenged before this Court, 
came to be affirmed with the dismissal on 29.03.2016 of 
the Special Leave Petition preferred by the appellant(s). 
5. Learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant(s) 
has sought to distinguish the case of the respondent(s) 
herein viz a viz the employees who have been granted the 
benefit of the above referred lis but we are of the considered 
view that there is no such distinction which can be culled 
out in the particular facts and circumstances of this case. 

--- Page 323 ---
C.A. No.  7871 OF 2024          3 
6. We, therefore, dismiss the present appeal in the 
peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case. 
7. Pending applications(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (C)  No.10446/2025
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated  10-09-2024
in MATA No. 129/2018 passed by the High Court of Orissa at Cuttack]
DEEPAK KUMAR BEHERA                                Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
SUCHISMITA BEHERA                                  Respondent(s)
[TO BE TAKEN UP IN THE COMMITTEE ROOM IN THE SECOND SESSION] 
[MEDIATION REPORT RECEIVED] 
(IA No. 84019/2025 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.)
 
Date : 01-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE J.B. PARDIWALA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K. VINOD CHANDRAN
For Petitioner(s) : 
Mr. Deepak Kumar Behera
                   Mr. Naresh Kumar- 1271, AOR
                   Mr. Gautam Kumar Laha, Adv.
                   Mr. Santosh Kumar Mishra, Adv.                  
                   
For Respondent(s) : Ms. Jahnavi Taneja, AOR                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The appellant is aggrieved with the refusal of the Trial Court
to grant him divorce for reason of the appellant having not proved
that the respondent was guilty of desertion. The High Court by the
impugned order confirmed the decision of the Trial Court.
3. The appellant was married to the respondent in the year 2012.
The appellant asserts that the marriage lasted only for six months
and then they separated. Since then, or even before, the appellant
alleges that there was no conjugal relationship between the couple

--- Page 325 ---
2
and the respondent had eventually deserted him. The respondent, on
the other hand, contended that they fell in love and got married
and for three years, they had lived without any problems. It is due
to the recalcitrant attitude of the appellant that she had to leave
the matrimonial home and even now she is ready to go back.
4. Considering the long separation, we were apprehensive whether
any useful purpose would be served in continuing the relationship,
hence we directed the parties to remain present before us for
interaction in the Committee Room. Today, when the matter was
called, we were informed that the appellant is present in person
and the respondent is available online.
5. We heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned
Amicus Curiae for the respondent.
6. The learned Amicus Curiae on behalf of the respondent asserted
that  the  respondent  is  willing  to  go  back  to  resume  the
relationship.  However,  the  learned  counsel  for  the  appellant
submits that there could be no matrimony continued.
7. We  interacted  with  the  appellant  and  the  respondent
separately.  We were of the definite opinion that there is
irretrievable breakdown of the marriage, despite the fact that the
respondent was insisting to resume the relationship.  There are no
children in the wedlock and in the facts and circumstances, it is
befitting that the parties be left to live their lives separately.
8. Now, the only question before us was with respect to the
alimony payable.  The appellant is employed as a Manager (Mining)
in the Coal India Limited. The appellant submits that he had
already paid Rs.15 lakhs to the respondent and he is willing to pay
a lumpsum amount of Rs.15 lakhs more for an amicable separation.
The appellant also points out that he has been facing multiple
issues due to his ailing parents, one of them, his father, having
passed away recently after a prolonged illness. His mother is also
bedridden, and he is taking care of her.
9. The appellant, on our persuasion was inclined to raise the
amount of alimony to Rs.20 lakhs, but we are of the opinion that
Rs.25 lakhs should be paid to the respondent-wife by the appellant.

--- Page 326 ---
3
The appellant seeks three months’ time for payment of the said
amount.
10. In such circumstances, we are inclined to grant the said
period to the appellant for deposit of the amounts directed by us;
on  deposit  of  which,  we  could  invoke  Article  142  of  the
Constitution of India to dissolve the marriage between the parties
on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage. Only to
facilitate  the  deposit  and  disbursal  of  the  amount  to  the
respondent, we direct the appellant to deposit Rs.25 lakhs before
the Registry of this Court within a period of three months.
11. Post the matter on 05.01.2027 at 3.30 p.m. in the Committee
Room as part-heard.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                    (POOJA SHARMA)
DEPUTY REGISTRAR                                 COURT MASTER (NSH)

3. Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioners,

the petitioners within two weeks from today, failing which

1. This court in an earlier order dated 25.03.2026, had
directed the concerned High Court to take up Criminal
Appeal No.532 of 2022 pending before it and to dispose it
of within 6 months of the date of order. It has been
brought to our notice that the Appeal preferred by the
Petitioner in the year 2022 before the High Court is still
pending despite our direction on the matter.
2. In view of the aforementioned and taking into account
the fact that the Petitioner has undergone a sentence of 7
years and 9 months pending appeal, we are inclined to grant
bail to the Petitioner subject to conditions that the
jurisdictional Trial Court may deem fit to impose, pending
the final disposal of his appeal before the High Court.
Ordered accordingly.

is disposed of.

disposed of.

2.Delay condoned.
1

--- Page 542 ---
SLP(Crl. D.No.24861/2026
3.It appears that the petitioner is in judicial custody past
four years.  However, having regard to the nature of the crime
as alleged, we are not persuaded to exercise our discretion in
favour of the petitioner insofar as his plea for bail is
concerned.
4.We are informed that, till this date, four witnesses have been
examined.  Two witnesses are in box, their examination-in-chief
is over. In fact, we do not approve this practice of the Trial
Court adjourning the matter after recording of the examination-
in-chief.  Once the examination in chief is completed, the
defence counsel must start with the cross examination of that
witness.
5.Be that as it may.  We direct the Trial Court to ensure that
the trial is completed within a period of six months from today
without fail.
6.The disposal of the trial shall be reported to this Court.
7.With the aforesaid, the Special Leave Petition stands disposed
of.
8.Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
